radius.$description: Border radius scale for johnthedesigner.com. Personality: rounded-but-controlled — warm and approachable without being consumer-playful. Scale approved in style-preview v5. Hierarchy principle: inline interactive elements (6px) < containers (10px) < overlays (18px). No component uses the same radius as a component at a meaningfully different scale. Full-radius reserved for badges and pills only.

none.$description: Hard edge. Use for: horizontal rules, full-bleed image containers, code block backgrounds where content must align flush, data table cells. Not used on interactive elements.

xs.$description: Minimal rounding. Use for: inline code snippets, small chip variants, tooltip containers. Barely perceptible — signals precision without being sharp.

sm.$description: INTERACTIVE TIER — primary radius for all interactive inline elements. Use for: buttons (all variants), text inputs, select controls, semantic state blocks (error/success/warning), search fields. 6px creates a friendly but controlled feel appropriate to a professional portfolio.

md.$description: General purpose. Use for: image thumbnails in flowing content, inline media embeds at small scale, secondary surface elements that need moderate rounding. Bridges interactive (6px) and container (10px) tiers.

lg.$description: CONTAINER TIER — primary radius for surface containers. Use for: work index cards, media embeds, image panels, aside containers. Cards use shadow-sm for elevation — radius is the shape complement to that shadow.

xl.$description: PANEL TIER — solid section panels and prominent callouts. Use for: blue-500 callout blocks, CTA sections (blue-500 or slate-900 fills), featured aside blocks. Larger containers warrant more rounding to avoid feeling like sharp-cornered rectangles at their size.

2xl.$description: OVERLAY TIER — highest radius in the system. Use for: modals, dialogs, drawers, bottom sheets. The soft rounding of overlays communicates their temporary/floating nature. Do not apply to persistent UI elements.

full.$description: PILL — full circular radius. Use for: badges (solid and outline), tags, filter chips. Pill shapes are high-emphasis visual signals — reserved for these labeling components only. Do not apply full-radius to buttons, cards, or inputs — it would conflict with the system's controlled-rounding personality.

shadow.$description: Elevation scale. Three levels only — minimal shadow system. Shadow colors derived from slate-900 (#0e1720) hue for cool-tinted shadows rather than generic black-opacity. Solid fill sections (blue-500, slate-900) use no shadow — color carries the emphasis.

none.$description: No elevation. Use for: flat bordered elements (dividers, bordered cards before hover), inline code, page-level surface. Pair with border-color token for visible structure without elevation.

sm.$description: Raised surface. Use for: work index cards, any surface that must visually lift off the page. The second shadow value below (1px hairline) is expressed as a separate CSS layer: 0 0 1px rgba(14,23,32,0.06). Both layers should be applied together: box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(14,23,32,0.08), 0 0 1px rgba(14,23,32,0.06)

sm-hairline.$description: Hairline layer — always paired with shadow.sm. Creates a subtle edge definition at the border of raised cards. Apply as the second value in a multi-layer box-shadow declaration.

lg.$description: Overlay elevation. Use for: modals, dialogs, dropdown menus, tooltip panels. The second layer: 0 2px 8px rgba(14,23,32,0.07). Full declaration: box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(14,23,32,0.14), 0 2px 8px rgba(14,23,32,0.07)

lg-mid.$description: Mid layer — always paired with shadow.lg. Apply as the second value in a multi-layer box-shadow declaration.

focus-ring.$description: Focus ring glow — paired with a 2px solid blue-500 border on focused inputs. Creates a soft blue halo that reinforces focus visibility beyond the border alone. Full input focus declaration: border: 2px solid #1683FF; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(22,131,255,0.18)

border.$description: Border width tokens. Kept minimal — this system favors solid fills and shadows over borders as structural elements. Borders appear only where a dividing line genuinely communicates structure.

none.$description: No border. Default for elevated surfaces — shadow provides definition.

sm.$description: Standard border. Use for: horizontal rules (hr), section dividers, flat card outlines, input resting state. The majority of bordered elements.

md.$description: Medium border. Use for: badge-outline variant border, ghost button border. Slightly heavier than sm to ensure visibility at small sizes.

lg.$description: Heavy border. Use for: focused input border (blue-500, 2px), active/selected state indicators. Signals interactivity.

focus.$description: Focus ring border width. Applied as border: 2px solid color.border-focus on focused interactive elements. Always paired with shadow.focus-ring.
